title: SRE on-call scratchpad — paging notes & follow-ups
content:
2026-03-04 — Oncall scratchpad (Sam R)
Shift: 06:00 - 14:00 PT

Quick context
- Week after deploy: rolling update of prefix-cache service (v2) started last night. Ops dashboard showed some 5xx spikes and increased CPU on a subset of nodes starting ~01:30 UTC.
- Pager at 07:12 PT from PagerDuty: high error rate on /embeddings route (latency + 500s).

Pages / incidents (chronological)
1) 07:12 PT — Page: embeddings 5xx spike (PD alert: endpoint-error-rate > 2% for 5m)
   - First response: ack 07:13, jumped into logs and SLO dashboard.
   - Observed: error surge correlated with two hosts in prefix-cache pool (pc-23, pc-24). Both show OOM-killed container restarts around 01:25 UTC and then rapid CPU oscillation.
   - Actions: put pc-23 and pc-24 into maintenance (drain) via console routing policy, traffic routed to fallback model group (smaller instance type).
   - Mitigation status: errors dropped to baseline by 07:21. Alert closed at 07:30.
   - Notes: client impact limited due to fallback routing but 99th p90 latency increased ~120ms for affected requests.

2) 09:05 PT — Follow-up from SRE-4823 (postmortem kickoff)
   - Created JIRA SRE-4823 to track root cause + remediation (owner: @Ethan Park). Summary copied below.

Observations / hypotheses
- Symptoms point to memory regression in v2 of prefix-cache when handling large-context keys > 64k tokens (edge-case workload from internal eval).
- OOM restarts on pc-23/24 preceded high error-rate; those pods receive disproportionate long-seq requests. Might be missing prefix-eviction config for v2.
- Autoscaler did not react quickly because pod CPU spiked but memory stayed above threshold until OOM. Need mem-based scaling or earlier soft-kill.

Immediate follow-ups (todo, short-term)
- [ ] Add eviction/upper-bound flag to v2 prefix-cache (config change) — owner: @Ethan (Ethan will prototype safe default). Target: deploy canary by 2026-03-06.
- [x] Drain pc-23/24 and replace with pc-25/26 (done 07:18 PT) — note: replacement nodes healthy.
- [ ] Add memory usage alert (pod mem > 75% for 3m) to supplement CPU based autoscaling — owner: @Sam (me).
- [ ] Add a temporary rate-limit for internal evals to prevent large-context abuse while v2 stabilizes — owner: @Mia.
- [ ] Post-incident load test to reproduce long-context OOM pattern (run locally with eval dataset) — owner: infra-qe (assign in ticket).

Runbook TODOs (needs updates)
- Existing runbook "prefix-cache-oom" (Confluence) is outdated for v2 behavior. Tasks:
  - [ ] Update runbook with v2-specific debugging steps (how to inspect KV cache sizes, eviction counters, env flags) — owner: @Sam.
  - [ ] Add explicit instructions for safe draining + rolling restart for capacity pools that serve model-variants.
  - [ ] Include sample k8s mem/cpu thresholds recommended for mCPU heavy workloads.

Paging notes (for next oncall)
- If alert is triggered: check `k8s events` for OOMKill before looking at CPU. OOMKill will often show in node events.
- Use routing console to route traffic to fallback-model-group (route name: embeddings-fallback) instead of immediate restart of prefix-cache pods.
- Do not restart entire pool at once; rotate one node at time and watch error rate for 5m window.

Follow-up items for platform/dev (medium-term)
- Investigate making autoscaler memory-aware for prefix-cache pools (proposal doc link TBD).
- Add a workload classifier to routing to detect long-context evals and steer them to a dedicated pool or throttled queue.
- Evaluate quantization/encoding changes in v2 that might increase memory per KV entry.

Open questions / unknowns
- Why did only pc-23/24 see OOMs? Are those nodes on different instance type or had different eviction thresholds? Need node-level inventory.
- Is there a regression in v2's KV encoding leading to larger memory usage per item? (run binary diffs, check serialization code)

Notes to self (quick reminders)
- Draft short postmortem skeleton in SRE-4823 today (outline: summary, timeline, root cause, action items, owners).
- Sync with Ethan after his config PR is ready; coordinate canary window (low traffic).
- Add mem-based alert before end of shift (put in monitoring draft).

Misc small ops tasks done
- Renewed kube node-label rule for prefix-cache pools (forgot to propagate after last infra terraform run) — verified change applied.
- Updated local runbook snippet for how to force drain with `--delete-local-data` for sticky test nodes.

End-of-shift handoff (for afternoon oncall)
- Handoff to @Mia Li at 14:00 PT.
- Slack DM summary queued + link to SRE-4823.
- Make sure mem-alert PR is at least opened + assigned before leaving.

Snippets to paste into ticket/postmortem
- Timeline (short): 01:25 UTC pod OOMs (pc-23/24) -> 07:12 PT alert triggered by increased 5xxs -> 07:18 PT drained affected nodes -> 07:21 PT error rate returned to baseline.
- Immediate remediation: drained affected nodes and routed traffic to embeddings-fallback; replacement nodes healthy.

End notes (informal)
- Rough day but good fallback routing did its job — minimize customer impact.
- Need to treat long-context evals as a separate workload; current pool assumptions on average key size don't hold for internal eval runs.

-- Sam
